summary: 11/15 harnesses compiled and linked. KLEE ran on all 11 but found 0 real bugs. One false positive in fuzz_nm (KLEE aborted on unmodeled external call get_file_size→stat). Most harnesses use file-based I/O (write symbolic data to temp file, open with BFD/nm), creating state too complex for KLEE to explore effectively. 4 harnesses failed to compile due to missing OSS-Fuzz build infrastructure.

harnesses.name: fuzz_addr2line
harnesses.failure_reason: KLEE timeout during bitcode optimization — 74MB combined.bc too large

harnesses.name: fuzz_as
harnesses.failure_reason: Missing fuzz_as.h — requires separate GAS (GNU Assembler) configure + build to generate

harnesses.name: fuzz_dlltool
harnesses.failure_reason: Undeclared identifier 'mname' in generated fuzz_dlltool.h — the sed-based header generation from dlltool.c is incomplete without DLLTOOL_I386 build context

harnesses.name: fuzz_dwarf
harnesses.failure_reason: OBJDUMP_PRIVATE_VECTORS expands to empty string literal '""' which causes 'called object type char[1] is not a function' error in fuzz_objdump.h

harnesses.name: fuzz_nm
harnesses.failure_reason: KLEE aborted on unmodeled external call get_file_size() at fuzz_nm.h:1641 — stat() syscall not supported. Not a real bug.

key_findings: 11/15 harnesses compiled and linked successfully against a 74MB LLVM bitcode of binutils (bfd + libiberty + opcodes)
KLEE ran on all 11 harnesses (42–525s each) but found 0 real bugs
1 false positive in fuzz_nm: KLEE aborted on unmodeled external call get_file_size() which calls stat() — not a memory safety bug
4 harnesses failed to compile due to generated headers from OSS-Fuzz build.sh (sed-patching tool sources into .h files)
OSS-Fuzz harnesses use file-based I/O (write symbolic bytes to temp file, open with BFD), creating state explosion that KLEE cannot explore
Even with all 15 available OSS-Fuzz harnesses and 300s KLEE timeout, B1 found 0 bugs on binutils vs SAILOR's 73
